**Black Lotus.** Many dark elves use Black Lotus as blade venom (see the **WFRP Core Rulebook** ). 

**Manbane** . One of the most lethal venoms formulated, manbane is made from the _lathranoi_ flower. It causes even the smallest cut to bleed copiously. If the target takes at least 1 Wound, take a **Difficult (−10) Endurance** Test or suffer 2 _Bleeding_ Conditions and 3 _Poisoned_ Conditions. 

**Sildru.** Known as ‘dark venom’, a blade venom derived from spiders, assassins use _sildru_ to cause drawn-out, agonising death. If a target takes at least 1 Wound, they must pass a **Hard (−20) Endurance** Test to avoid the _Unconscious_ Condition and 2 _Poisoned_ Conditions. 

## **Chariots**
Naggaroth’s roads are long and treacherous, passing through beast-haunted forests and across icy tundra, so dark elf travellers who want to reach their destination swiftly and safely use mounts to speed their travel and avoid spending a night in the wild. The wealthiest travellers use chariots, a legacy of life before the Sundering. Wagons and chariots pulled by dark steeds, similar to those described on page 76 of **Sea Wardens of Cothique** , offer protection from outlaws and monsters on a long journey, and their retainers can follow with any possessions they wish to bring. 

## **Scourgerunner Chariot**
Beastmasters ride in scourgerunner chariots when hunting swift-moving beasts across the fens and plains. Built to resemble a sleek boat, they run on a single central wheel, pulled along by dark steeds. Charioteers are armed with barbed nets and a Ravager Harpoon which they use to snare and immobilise their prey. 

## **Cold One Chariot**
**Valikh.** A rare blade venom used by the Brides of Burning Blood subcult of witch elves. If a target takes at least 1 Wound, their blood starts to boil. At the end of every subsequent Round, they suffer 1d10 Damage, ignoring AP, with a minimum of 1 Wound. The effect is removed if the target passes a **Difficult (–10) Endurance** Test at the beginning of a Round. 

**Vrasha.** A transparent, viscous fluid made from the saliva and slime oozing from the skin of a cold one or related reptile. Those who ride cold ones daub themselves in _vrasha_ to mask their own scent, so tthat he beast will then accept them as a rider. The liquid also numbs their flesh and sense of smell and taste. If used once, lose all sense of smell, taste, and touch and gain the _Painless_ Trait for 1d10 hours. After using 10 times, these effects are permanent. Poured onto an open wound, _vrasha_ immediately removes all _Bleeding_ Conditions and restores 2 Wounds, while inflicting 2 _Fatigued_ Conditions. 

**Witchbrew.** Distilled from the blood of hag queens, witchbrew is a rare libation used by Khainites to instill the ecstasy of destruction. Automatically induces _Frenzy_ and _Hatred (All)_ for 2d10 minutes. If all enemies are dead or gone, take a **Difficult (−10) Cool** Test or attack the nearest living creature. 

**Zha’Kheril.** ‘Ireleaf ’ is the most common potion mixed by death hags for witch elves to imbibe before battle. It grants +5 WS and +5 Ag. After wearing off, reduce WS and Ag by −5 each for a further hour. **Duration** : 1 hour. 

Cold one chariots are traditionally a gift from Malerion to knights or nobles who please him with their devotion. To possess one is a sign of prestige, even if the cold ones’ truculent nature can bring the chariot to a jarring halt at the most inopportune moments. 

## **Sailing Ships**
Dark elves are expert seafarers and their shipyards build swift, manoeuvrable vessels. They are not as accomplished as their Asur kin, perhaps over-reliant on black arks for sea power. 

## **Ravenship**
These are the most common warships in Druchii fleets, nimble galleys with two masts rigged with lateen sails. Their hulls are shaped into graceful lines with wing-like protrusions and timbers painted jet black. Ravenships mount two reaper batteries (6) on each side (12 in total) 

## **Storm Barque**
Larger and faster than a ravenship, the storm barque forgoes oars for an additional mast and less maneuverability. Storm barques were once a common sight in the Sea of Malice, though they grow steadily obsolete as more versatile vessels take precedence. Most originate from cities with limited maritime interests, such as Har Ganeth. Storm barques mount three reaper bolt thrower batteries (9) on each side (18 in total).
